Section B: Education

text: In modern industrial societies there are many views on the role of the family, marriage and kinship.
Family size has changed over time and today families can most accurately be described as diverse.
For some, marriage remains an essential part of family life, whereas for others it is optional.

Section C: Crime, deviance and social control

text: Education has an important influence on the lives of individuals, often affecting future life chances.
Differences in achievement can be due to a wide range of home and school factors. For example,
the type of school an individual attends is thought by many to be very influential.

Section D: Media

text: According to the official crime statistics, some social groups are more likely to commit crime than
others. There are many different explanations for this, one of which is the labelling theory. How
the law enforcement agencies deal with crime is also important. Criminals are punished in lots of
different ways today but all punishment aims to reduce crime rates in society.

text: Today there are more media products and technologies available to the audience than ever before,
resulting in increased interactivity. However, this does not mean that media owners are any less
powerful than they were previously. The role of the media in society and its ability to promote
certain norms and values is therefore frequently debated by sociologists.
